Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
In article <8h0ml5$d27$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,

tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> A political action is canceled via Telepatic Vote counting
> or with a Delaying Tactics.

> Is that vote considered "failed"?'

No. It is neither successful nor failed. It is simply canceled.
(Not that this matters much - most cards that would care about
the failed status of the referendum couldn't be played after the
thing was canceled anyhow)

Note: the action is still successful (unblocked), which matters
for some cards (like inferior Freak Drive after a Telepathic Vote
Counting).

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 30 May 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:

> A political action is canceled via Telepatic Vote counting
> or with a Delaying Tactics.
> Is that vote considered "failed"?

6.3.2.3 would suggest that it neither passes nor fails, since it never
reaches the resolution of the referendum phase.

"Resolve the referendum. If there are more votes for the referendum than
against, the referendum passes and the effects of the successful
referendum take place. Otherwise, the referendum fails and has no
effect. Tied referendums fail."
